summary:
# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: ADVENTURES OF BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins; author credited "Herbert Jenkins", Gutenberg says Jenkins, Herbert George)

**Front matter:** Bindle = Joseph Bindle, furniture remover. Book follows Bindle helping Mr Hearty advertise new shop; Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room turned into soldiers' billets; Mrs Bindle takes lodger; Bindle porter at Fulham Square Mansions letting same flat twice; Bindle discourages Rev. Andrew MacFie courting niece Millie Hearty. Recurring: Ginger (gloomy), Wilkes (always coughing), Huggles (grin), Lady Knob-Kerrick, Dick Little, "Guggers", Mr and Mrs Hearty, "Millikins". Dedication "To the Children of the Dead End". Other books by author: The Bindles on the Rocks, Bindle, The Night Club, John Dene of Toronto, Malcolm Sage, Mrs Bindle, Patricia Brent, The Return of Alfred, The Rain Girl, The Stiffsons.

**Setting:** Fenton Street, Fulham (Bindles' home, "little grey 'ome in the west"). Mrs Bindle = Lizzie. Married 19 years. Bindle wears blue-and-white cricket cap; special constable uniform. Bindle's pipe; beer from The Yellow Ostrich; "Drag and Hounds", "Green Lion", "Feathers", "Granville", "Ancient Earl", "Scarlet Horse" (Ruddy Bill's pub, lost private room).

**Ch I The Coming of the Lodger**
- Mrs Bindle serves stew, apple-pie. Ad in *The Gospel Sentinel*: "CHRISTIAN HOME wanted by a single gentleman, chapel-goer, temperance, quiet, musical, home-comforts, good-cooking, moderate terms... Apply Lonely."
- Bindle's "lodger" monologue (lodger = convention; "unejectable"). Anecdote of Horace Gaze (returns from front, enters back door).
- Lodger = Mr Josiah Gupperduck, plays accordion; "Society for the Suppression of Atheism" lecturer; "I am a sower of the seed"; "spiritual seed". Arrives Monday 8pm: small, thin, round spectacles, three wisps hair, short brown beard, red nose, ears like sign-boards, 3-day stubble. Bindle: "Looks like a owl wot's been on the drink."
- Bindle "puts an 'ead on the beer" from a yard away; "'Ere's long legs to the baby!" Bindle's "lemonade" jibe; "Gupperducks" pun.
- Bindle's song: "If You Squeeze Me Tighter, Jimmie, I Shall Scream" (from The Granville). Gupperduck refuses to play.
- Mrs Bindle: "You're a disgrace..." Bindle: "if you an' 'im start givin' each other the glad-eye... I'm 'ot stuff."
- Mr Hearty = greengrocer, married Mrs Bindle's sister (Martha). Mrs Hearty wheezes, "my breath".

**Ch II A Downing Street Sensation**
- Bindle, employed by Messrs Empsom & Daley (cartage), rides horse to Merton with Tippitt (weedy, cigarette on lip, "Married, mate!"). Stable-hand Spotty gives leg-up. Bindle slides off; walks; drinks at Drag and Hounds; catches bus; sleeps on Wimbledon Common.
- Pantechnicon from John Smith & Co., Merton; two ladies (sallow older woman with pince-nez; younger driver smiles, freezes at Bindle's wink). Destination: Mr Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street, "carved-oak dining-room furniture". Key handed over by a lady near Houses of Parliament.
- Man on road: van full of suffragettes, white dresses, coloured sashes. Bindle: "air-'oles" in van roof.
- Bindle buys lamp-black (oil-shop, Wimbledon High St; pea-puffer, half-crown tested by girl). Waters van from Green Lion watering-can; pumps lamp-black through roof holes. Tippitt gets drinks.
- Bindle tells Downing St inspector: "Joseph Bindle's my name. I'm a special, Fulham district."
- Doors opened: ~20 "Black and White Raiders" (Votes for Women), lamp-black smeared. Tippitt knocked down, cigarette falls. Mr Llewellyn John watches from window. Girl with mirror hysterics. Crowd jeers ("Soap for Women!"). Constables herd them to Whitehall; taxi drivers refuse; women go by Tube/District.
- Chief-Inspector Gunny (Scotland Yard, suffragist head). Deputy-Commissioner gives Bindle a cigar. Gunny: "If at any time I can help you, let me know."

**Ch III The Air-Raid**
- I: Bindle at Heartys' during raid. Gupperduck "I have no fear of earthly things." Mr Hearty and Gupperduck hide in potato-cellar. Bindle: "a shillin' rabbit." Bindle leaves; Millie: "You know you are the only Uncle Joe I've got." Millie's sweetheart Charlie Dixon, Sergeant, 110th Service Bn London Regt, at front.
- II: Bindle drops scales (7 lbs weights) on trap-door, scares them; Mrs Bindle faints. Gupperduck loses spectacles and upper false teeth. Bindle: "Wot about you puttin' your trust in Gawd?" Mrs Hearty laughs.

**Ch IV The Duplication of Mr Hearty**
- I: Mrs Bindle: "You've never been a real husband to me." Stewed-steak-and-onions. Bindle: "Gawd made me, an' Gawd made 'Earty... in one of us 'E made a bloomer." Hearty opening third shop in Putney High St. Bindle visits Dr Richard "Dick" Little (Chelsea flat), with brother Tom Little, and Guggers (Captain, Gordons, "gug-gug", 14 stone; nickname Spit-and-Speak). Plan: publicity "rag" to advertise Hearty.
- II: Six duplicates of Hearty ("alibis") enter Putney shop, each says "Good afternoon, Joseph." Smith (right-hand man) hides in cellar. Errand boy Billy Nips. Mrs Hearty laughs silently on sack of potatoes. Hearty: "I give these men in charge." Duplicates march out playing tin whistles ("Men of Harlech" for one).
- Hearty: "Ahead... 'Earty's 'Eart."

**Ch V The Gathering of the Bands**
- Donkeys with boards advertising "ALFRED HEARTY THE NAPOLEON OF GREENGROCERS", "THE CAESAR OF FRUITERERS", "PRINCE OF POTATO MERCHANTS", "HEARTY'S TWO-SHILLING PINEAPPLE TRY IT IN YOUR BATH", "HEARTY'S JERUSALEM ARTICHOKES GENERAL ALLENBY EATS THEM", "HEARTY'S FRENCH BEANS SAVED VERDUN", "THEY CURE BALDNESS", "ALFRED HEARTY KNOWN AS PINEAPPLE ALF", "IF YOU DON'T BUY YOUR VEGETABLES... YOU WILL BE WHAT I AM". Vegetable-headed men lead donkeys.
- Camel: "I'VE GOT THE HUMP THROUGH NOT BUYING HEARTY'S VEGETABLES"; "EAT HEARTY'S LEEKS THEY DEFY THE PLUMBER". Camel roars.
- Bands: "Pull for the Shore, Sailor" (Hearty's favourite hymn; leader Charlie w/ cornet, drummer Ted), "Onward Christian Soldiers", "Shall We Gather at the River", "Gospel Bells", "The Last Noel", other bands; drum stuck on stairs (Ted, Striker). Little leader with green-and-yellow caps. Inspector stops traffic; summons threatened. Bindle: "advertisement's advertisement... this is obstruction."
- Mrs Bindle: "That Bindle's done this... It'll kill Mr. Hearty."

**Ch VI Mr Gupperduck's Mishap**
- Mrs Bindle: food shortages (2 candles, ¼ lb margarine). Bindle reports Hearty's court case. Bindle describes Regent's Park atheist meetings (khaki soldiers, "Oh, Cuthbert, don't!").
- Gupperduck late; found beaten: black eye, broken lip, blood on ear; brought by two friends: sandy-bearded man (weedy, cloth cap; "Peter") and little man with very long beard ("Wayskin"). Gupperduck had spoken at Hyde Park peace meeting to wounded soldiers. Bindle pours brandy; Mrs Bindle: "He's temperance."
- Bindle: "Camelflage" threat; "I'd sooner 'ave a flea than a soul."

**Ch VII The Courting of the Rev. Andrew MacFie**
- MacFie (Scottish, sandy, gloomy; sister Miss MacFie) pursues Millie. Millie left home to avoid Hearty; Hearty had insulted her re Charlie.
- Temperance Fete at Barton Bridge: lemonade spiked with alcohol (Bindle's doing); Lady Knob-Kerrick washed out of carriage by hose; MacFie led assault; "lemon-and-a-mac" drink named after him.
- Lady Knob-Kerrick nominated MacFie as Alton Road Chapel minister, replacing Rev. Mr Sopley.
- MacFie calls on Mrs Bindle in kitchen; Bindle enters singing "I'd rather Kiss the Mistress than the Maid." Millie: "I understood."
- Bindle to Hearty: "that sandy-'aired son of a tub-thumper." Sunday supper: Bindle asks about David & Uriah; Millie: "If I had been her... I should have killed David." Gupperduck's accordion E-sharp. Bindle leaves whistling "The Long, Long Trail."

**Ch VIII The Chapel Conversazione**
- Alton Road Chapel school-room; Mr Sopley's farewell (illuminated address, £50 purse, silver-mounted hot-water bottle). Texts "Prepare to Meet Thy God", "The Wages of Sin is Death", "And So Shall Ye All Likewise Perish."
- Guests: Mr and Mrs Pain (Alice mis-announces); Mr and Mrs Withers; Mr Tuddenham (red-faced) and Mr Muskett (lantern jaws); Miss Torkington (snubbed by Bindle); Mr and Mrs Gash; Mr Hippitt ("Mr Pip-Pip"); Mrs Muspratt ("Miss Musk-Rat"). Alice = maid.
- Glee-party sings "THE GLAD EYE" (Lady Knob-Kerrick outraged). Lady Knob-Kerrick, Miss Strint (companion), John (footman) with police-whistle.
- Woman (later Private "Nancy" Dane, actor, Passchendaele Pierrots) claims MacFie as husband "Andy"; MacFie denies. John blows whistle: "It's a raid!" Bindle: "It's ole Calves with that bloomin' police-whistle."
- Dick Little's flat afterwards; Dane removes wig (black toque). Bindle: "'e got the wind up proper."
- Magistrate dismisses summonses against Lady K-K and John. MacFie offers £20 reward (advertisement).

**Ch IX The Letting of Number Six**
- Mrs Bindle: "An' what am I to do if there's an air-raid?" Bindle leaves Harridge's Stores removal dept to be caretaker at Fulham Square Mansions while Charlie Hart (Harts' Mrs Hart ill) takes holiday.
- Mrs Sedge (Charlie Hart's mother-in-law, gin "Royal Richard", bonnet). Charlie Hart: "'E's gone to the damned seaside."
- Number Seven (choleric ex-Indian civil servant; "damned"). Number Eight maid "Queenie" (shrewish; Bindle ignores). Number Twelve (Fluffles, Pekinese). Number Eleven (quiet old lady, postage stamp).
- Number Six let to Miss Cissie Boye (revue "Kiss Me Quick", Regent Theatre) and Mr Jabez Stiffson (rent 3½ guineas/week; wife away; bird Oscar, canary).
- Bindle wears special's uniform to avoid complaints.

**Ch X The Downfall of Mr Jabez Stiffson**
- Mrs Sedge: "She's got an 'ead-piece on 'er." Miss Boye in bath; Stiffson in pink bath-robe. Bindle: "There's been a little mistake."
- Breakfast (coffee, eggs, bacon, strawberry jam). Mrs Stiffson arrives ("Jabez!", "tweed mixture"); Stiffson's coffee down waistcoat.
- Mrs Stiffson hurls bowl of porridge on Stiffson's head. Stiffson's luggage and Oscar flee. Mrs Stiffson shrieks "Police", gets stuck in lift; Bindle: "fate and the lift had joined the Entente against Mrs. Stiffson."

**Ch XI The Camouflaging of Mr Gupperduck**
- Yellow Ostrich bar: Ginger ("I don't 'old wiv war"; spits), Wilkes, Huggles. Bindle: "Llewellyn John... no dinner-hour"; Haig/George V anecdote joke.
- Mrs Bindle asks about Gupperduck. Bindle: Gupperduck's Peace meeting attack on Hyde Park; "Peter" the sandy-beard man up a tree; Wayskin ran off, trousers gone; "I'll camelflage 'im."
- Mrs Bindle: "Gupperduck... not come back to my place"; Bindle: "peace wot passes all understandin'."

**Ch XII The Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino**
- Scratcher (lantern-jaw, fishy eyes) gets Bindle job as waiter at Napolini's, Regent Street. Waiters' tips; "bouillabaisse de Marseilles, pommes sautees."
- Bindle nicknames Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino "Kayser"; Italian fury. Tolmenicino knocks waiter with bottle; soup, whitebait, macaroni flying. He rams chief superintendent Herr James Smith (formerly Herr Siegesmann; Dundreary whiskers; 60, 25 years service): "Berlice!"
- Caille en casserole fiasco (lady, Welsh rarebit). Champagne in hot water (wine-cooler), cork hits monocle, soup, customers. Bindle discharged.
- Tolmenicino charged at Marlborough Street under Defence of the Realm Act; spy documents. Vine Street police station. Bindle: "So the Lodger Pawned His Second Pair of Boots."

**Ch XIII The Return of Charlie Dixon**
- Millie: Charlie's back; Universal Cafe with band; Bindle hesitates, then comes; Bindle orders asparagus joke; champagne "Number 68" (Millie's first drink).
- Charlie proposes; Millie to marry before he returns to front in ten days. Bindle: "Are you goin' to send this 'ere boy back to France un'appy?" Bindle to Hearty: "you're up against the biggest thing in your life."
- Millie: "I wish I could give every girl an Uncle Joe." Charlie grips Bindle's hand: "Your friendship 'urts like 'ell."

**Ch XIV Mr Hearty Yields**
- Mrs Bindle: "Look at 'Earty." Bindle in uniform visits Hearty. Hearty refuses to permit marriage (Millie not 20). Bindle invents tale: Hearty's old "pal" (Six-an'-Eightpence) will "go to the Ole Bird on the 'Ill" to expose Hearty; Hearty surrenders. Millie: "Oh, Uncle Joe, you darling!" Bindle: "I wonder if they'll charge me up with that little fairy tale."

**Ch XV A Billeting Adventure**
- Harridge's pantechnicon: Bindle, Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles. Lady Knob-Kerrick's house The Poplars, Putney Hill. Footman John (plush and calves). Butler Mr Wilton; housekeeper Mrs Marlings (black silk, cameo locket).
- Delivery-note: 16 bedsteads, bedding, four baths, washstands. Bindle: "We're 'ere to turn the Ole Bird's drawin'-room into billets for soldiers."
- Bindle places Wilkes's hat on bust of Sir Benjamin Biggs.
- Ginger's red herring burnt; Mrs Marlings: "hit will poison us."
- Sixteen soldiers with sergeant arrive. Lady K-K: "Billet sixteen soldiers!" Bindle: "You got 'various' veins in your legs, mum?" Ginger's aside "I seen 'im!"
- Lady K-K orders them removed; Bindle: "Are we downhearted?" "Noooo!" Huggles says "Here we are again."
- Bindle: "'Ow Mr. Little... my ole Dick" ("Beats me does Mr. Little")—Bindle's happy ending.

**Ch XVI Millie's Wedding**
- Mrs Bindle complains of Bindle's crush-hat and cigar. Bindle to Mrs Bindle: "Millikins... means an 'ell of a lot to me." Mrs Bindle's disappointment.
- Mr Hearty's carriage door mishap; Hearty's hat chased under carriage; he steps on dog's paw.
- Millie married by Rev. Mr Sopley (from Eastbourne; refuses MacFie). Bindle gives first kiss.
- Breakfast: Mr John Dixon (bridegroom's uncle) asks for beer; Hearty: "We are temperance." Bindle's Bible joke ("lorst the cup"; "The Pink 'Un").
- Bindle's speech: marriage "made in Fulham"; "bottles is returnable... you can't return your missus."
- Taxi takes couple off. Mrs Dixon: "Mr Bindle... you must be a very good man." Bindle and Mr Dixon walk toward Putney Bridge.
- END.

## BOOK 2: THE RED DERELICT (Bertram Mitford; Methuen 1904; Gutenberg 36588)

**Ch 1 The Episode of the Brindled Gnu**
- Wagram Gerard Wagram, Hilversea Court (park, Hilversea), enjoys possession ("Mine!"). Past life bitter; now at peace.
- Rabbit rifle; adder spared. Old stone bridge, water-ouzels, mill.
- African antelopes kept in park; a blue wildebeeste (brindled gnu) escapes; chases girl on bicycle along park road toward gate. Girl falls, bicycle smashed by gnu's horns.
- Wagram grabs horns, lifted, tossed; girl shoots gnu with his rifle (cartridge fell from his pocket). Gnu dies; she is Delia Calmour.

**Ch 2 Afterwards**
- Delia: "I saw the cartridges fall out of your pocket..." Wagram's torn waistcoat/hoof wound. Under-keeper Perrin; Hood (keeper); Bowles butcher from village. "Hilversea" offers to send her by brougham; she declines, walks home.
- Warren, Bassingham cycle shop, to supply hire bike.
- Wagram sees Father Gayle (chaplain, same age, cultured, humorous). Gayle: "I hope she won't make trouble."

**Ch 3 Father and Son**
- Old Squire Grantley Wagram (~80, ex-diplomat, tall, iron-grey moustache). Butler Rundle.
- Calmour: Major Calmour, retired veterinary, drinker, lives Siege House. Daughter's breach-of-promise settlement from Vance's eldest fool (Charlie Vance).
- Everard Wagram (half-brother, "bad lot", "Butcher Ned"); portrait; left home 10+ years earlier after scandal and felony; presumed dead; last heard in Australia; different mothers.
- Squire: "Calmour at Hilversea!? Pho!" Squire bets Wagram £5 acquaintance won't end.

**Ch 4 Siege House and Its Ways**
- Siege House named for siege of Delhi. Bob (Robert Calmour, clerk, Pownall & Skreet solicitors, raffish); Clytie (typist, beautiful, "Damages", slangy); Delia (blue eyes, Grecian profile, dark hazel-eyed; Delia is the shy one). Old Calmour drinks.
- Bob plans damages claim vs Wagram. Clytie: "Capture the man." Delia throws golosh at Bob. Wagram's ring at gate.

**Ch 5 A Surprise Visit**
- Clytie feigns surprise; Wagram calls on Delia (returns bicycle news); Delia's "shorthand"; Clytie types detective story. Old Calmour drunk, shouting at gate; Clytie orders coffee.

**Ch 6 A Solemnity**
- Corpus Christi octave procession at Hilversea: Priest's Walk (limes, Calvary), legend of headless martyr.
- Wagram master of ceremonies in cassock; girl Yvonne Haldane (golden hair, 16, flanked by tots). Monsignor Culham (old friend of Squire, tall, white hair).
- Delia joins; Wagram tells her Haldane's family (Haldane, daughter Yvonne, "rarely seen apart"). Yvonne: "Sunbeam" (Haldane's name for her). Post-card collections. Haldane: post-cards.
- Wagram tells Delia about the choir; "Pax" joke.

**Ch 7 Concerning a Derelict**
- Breakfast: Squire, Monsignor, Haldane. Haldane reads Rhodesian report (R.M.S. Rhodesian, lat 10°5'N, long 16°36'W; ~900–1000 tons; rusty red hull).
- Haldane's own sighting on Manchurian; skipper said "run full speed against a cliff."
- Yvonne goes trout-fishing with Hood; Wagram mention of "Red Derelict".

**Ch 8 Retribution—Sharp and Sore**
- Yvonne & Wagram bicycle to Pritchett's farm (Mrs Pritchett; husband brews beer). Yvonne at gate, Bob Calmour (cheap bicycle suit) insults her ("Toll").
- Wagram cuts ground-ash stick, thrashes Bob: "crawling cur." Bob threatens law (£1000 damages).
- Haldane wants to kill Bob; Wagram: "I cut his small-clothes to ribbons."

**Ch 9 "We Get No Show."**
- Bob, Clytie, Delia; butcher Wells pesters for account; Pownall and Skreet. Clytie: "Here we are, two devilish good-looking girls... we get no show." Clytie's scheme: Delia to "capture the man."
- Clytie says Delia is "handicapped by genuineness."

**Ch 10 At Haldane's**
- Delia visits Haldanes (11 miles). Yvonne's Angora cat "Poogie". Post-card albums; Yvonne's portrait card. Haldane: "Pity she comes of that rotten brood."
- Delia meets Wagram on road; he is icy (he has heard Bob's claim). Delia gripped with confusion.

**Ch 11 Concerning Two Claims**
- Squire & Wagram receive Pownall & Skreet letter claiming £1000 for Delia (gnu) and £1000 for Bob (assault). Wagram decides to pay Delia's claim (sends cheque). Refuses Bob's.
- Delia wheels home; Bob mocks; Clytie sends them away.

**Ch 12 Concerning Two Claimants**
- Delia gets registered letter with cheque for £1000 (Grantley Wagram). She announces she will return it; Bob punctures bicycles; Calmour: "highly respectable firm."
- Pownall: Wagram's letter of 23rd June 1897 refusing Bob's claim; Wagram threatens Haldane's wrath.

**Ch 13 Concerning One Claim**
- Delia tears cheque, goes to Hilversea. Squire & Wagram. Priest's hiding-place (secret stone block, "martyr relative" portrait at Salamanca, St Omer).
- Delia wants to be a Catholic (Wagram suggests Father Sonnenbloem, Bassingham mission).

**Ch 14 The Sea and Her Dead**
- Newspaper: "A Terrible Tale of the Sea": steamship *Carboceer* sunk by derelict; survivor "Develin Hunt" (West African trader, ~60 years). Wagram: "There can't be two Develin Hunts."
- Haldane's joke: "Develin him." Tramp (swarthy, beady-eyed) asks for money; Wagram gives half-crown.

**Ch 15 More Siege House Amenities**
- Father drunk; Bob insinuates. Delia tells Bob that she recognises Miss Haldane's portrait; Bob is the man who insulted Yvonne.
- Editor of *The Old Country Side* commissions Delia to write article with photos of Hilversea (Wagram's doing). Clytie gets typing work.

**Ch 16 "A Calmour at Hilversea"**
- Delia at Hilversea; Rundle guides; photos of African animals (gnus, sable antelope); thunderstorm; Delia asks about conversion; Father Sonnenbloem.
- Delia plays organ; Arcadelt Ave Maria with Yvonne, Haldane, Wagram. Gerard (Wagram's son, 14).

**Ch 17 Blackmail?**
- Squire receives visit from Develin Hunt (white beard, adventurer). Hunt demands money; threatens Everard's involvement. Squire says he is an escaped lunatic; Hunt: "Blackmail, felony" threat; "your son Wagram... knows nothing."

**Ch 18 Further Counsels**
- Monsignor Culham: Squire confesses first wife's first marriage; Develin Hunt is Wagram's mother's earlier husband; Culham: obtain "documentary proof"; "give him rope."
- Wagram learns Develin Hunt staying at Golden Crown, Bassingham.

**Ch 19 Interim—Peace!**
- Summer Sunday; Delia plays organ; Gerard, Reggie; Gerard speaks of his father. Wagram & family leave for grouse on Thursday.
- Develin Hunt trespasses, Wagram greets him.

**Ch 20 A Forced Hand**
- Bob drunk at Golden Crown; Develin Hunt throws him out; Haldane almost knocks Bob down. Landlord Smith. Hunt learns Haldane's name.

**Ch 21 The Bolt**
- Develin Hunt demands £30,000 (accepts £25,000 cheque). Squire agrees. Wagram overhears through open window. Hunt reveals: Wagram's mother was married to Hunt before; so Wagram not legitimate.

**Ch 22 "Nobody of Nowhere"**
- Certificate from county-town parish register. Cheque placed in Wagram's hand; Squire urges destroying it. Hunt says Everard is in Lourenço Marques/Swaziland; Everard = "Butcher Ned," in gun-running. Hunt wants a handshake; Wagram shakes it.

**Ch 23 After the Blow**
- Squire explains; new will leaves personalty to Wagram; "Wagram Gerard, known as Wagram Gerard Wagram." Squire: "give Time his chance." Wagram resolves to find Everard.
- Gypsy hag at lane; Delia there; "green seas... battered ship... great happiness" prophecy.

**Ch 24 "Requiem Aeternam"**
- Squire dies (asleep). Monsignor Culham sings High Mass; Wagram's grief. Delia takes instruction; Wagram urges her to play music at Bassingham mission.
- Gossip about Wagram's refusal to remarry.

**Ch 25 The Red Derelict**
- SS *Baleka* (Captain Lawes), homeward from West Africa; passengers incl. Mrs Colville (widow, daughter Lily), Wagram (passenger, cabin to himself). Smoking-room debate: "we can't do evil that good may come of it."
- Derelict sighted; fourth officer Ransome calls it "Red Derelict."

**Ch 26 An Omen**
- Dinner: Mrs Colville superstitious; engines stop (propeller shaft snapped). Wagram: "Is that ill luck?"

**Ch 27 A Sacrifice in Vain**
- *Baleka* sinks (leak, watertight doors jam). Rockets. Lily missing; Wagram goes below; Mrs Colville faints. Captain Lawes forced into boat by crew; Ransome insubordination.
- Child Lily found safe in boat with mother. Wagram lost.

**Ch 28 The Rusted Pistol**
- Wagram in water, clings to deckchair; shark bites chair; he climbs on derelict (Red Derelict again).
- Finds rusted five-shot revolver with nameplate "E.W." (Everard's, given by Wagram).
- Sleeps; derelict drifts. Hulk sighted by *Baleka* survivors: Ransome: "that damned Red Derelict."

**Ch 29 A Break-up at Bassingham**
- Wagram's quest described (Lourenço Marques, Australia). Delia's grief. Gerard: "I wish he'd come back."
- Clytie's typing scheme; Haldane helps. Calmour dies of stroke. Haldane attends funeral. Calmour family moves to London.

**Ch 30 Concerning a Terror**
- Wagram wakes in native hut (cannibal tribe; tall men with spiky wool). A white man arrives. Two savages cut Wagram; he's held; a slaughter-yard.

**Ch 31 A Dark Place of the Earth**
- Wagram explores forest; a fetish enclosure with skulls on gate; sacrificial stone; a man stabbed by unseen hand.

**Ch 32 The Open Door**
- White renegade (rough, fierce, scar round right eye); offers ransom (£10,000 → £15,000). Shows slaughter-yard; "I'm God here." Wagram signs agreement; renegade sees name "Wagram Gerard Wagram" and rages.

**Ch 33 The Closed Door**
- Renegade tears up agreement; torments Wagram; forces him to watch human slaughter; Wagram saves a victim (black man), cuts bonds, holds at bay.
- Renegade "promise" to spare the man.

**Ch 34 The Alternative**
- Renegade wants Gerard brought out; Wagram refuses ("I will die first"). Wagram nearly killed at block; renegade postpones.

**Ch 35 Rout**
- Night: Wagram freed (by friendly black man). Given revolver. Joins attack on town; Maxim gun by renegade. Town burned. Wagram flees alone. Meets rescued man (friend).

**Ch 36 On the Great Deep**
- Wagram and savage companion's canoe journey; coast; Wagram in canoe alone. Finds the Red Derelict again; box found in bunk (tin case); skeleton pistol. Canoe lost.

**Ch 37 The Echo of a Prophecy**
- *Runic* (White Torpedo line) passes derelict; Delia sees man on deck; captain turns back; Wagram rescued. Delia looks after him.
- Delia recalls gipsy's prophecy: "great happiness."

**Ch 38 Time's Chance**
- Wagram at Hilversea; opens tin case: Develin Hunt marriage certificate (dated 4 years earlier to another woman, still alive); diary. Wagram thinks to blackmail Hunt.

**Ch 39 Time's Consummation**
- Haldane and Wagram find Hunt (now "Jack Faro") at Golden Crown, dying of motor accident (reported by *Bassingham Chronicle*). Hunt admits fraud; reveals Everard was the renegade ("Butcher Ned"); Wagram forgives. Jack Faro dies that night.

**Ch 40 Conclusion**
- Delia and Wagram at Hilversea; Wagram proposes; Delia accepts. Note: Red Derelict never sighted again.
